To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) the Pi/PPi system is critical for normal and abnormal mineralisation, (2) the Pi/Pyrophosphate (PP) system is critical for mineralisation, (3) the Pi/ PPi system is critical in the initiation and progression of a variety of mineralisation disorders, and (4) the Pi/ P system is critical for the initiation and progression in mineralisation disorders.
the Pi/PPi balance is regulated by the Pi/PPase and MV-related proteins and that the Pi/Pyrophosphate balance is regulated by Pi/PPase.
the phosphate/ pyrophosphate (Pi/PPi) balance is a critical regulator of biomineralisation in vivo, and that the Pi/PPi balance can be modulated by the action of the MV-related proteins.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the identification of the key factors that regulate the mineralisation of the extracellular matrix in the skeleton and in other tissues.
the identification and characterization of proteins that are critical in the process of mineralisation, and that are involved in the regulation of Pi/PP.
the identification, characterisation, and functional validation of novel proteins that regulate mineralisation.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
Pi is a key promoter of mineralisation, while PPi is a key inhibitor of mineralisation, and that the two are in a constant dynamic balance to regulate biomineralisation.
Pi/PPi and the MV-associated proteins (MVPs) are key players in the initiation, progression and termination of biomineralisation.
the Pi/PPi system has an important role in the regulation of biomineralisation and that the regulation of Pi/PPI levels is a key step in the control of biomineral formation and dissolution.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
Pi and PPi are critical in the control of mineral deposition in bone and cartilage.

the regulation of Pi/PPis homeostasis is essential for the control of biomineralisation and that this process is regulated by a number of genes, including the genes encoding the Pi/PPi transporter, Pi/PPi transporters, and the MV-related proteins.
the Pi/PPi balance is a critical factor in the initiation, progression and regulation of matrix mineralisation, and is essential for the development of normal bone and cartilage.
The main takeaway from our work is that
Pi/PPi are critical in mineralisation.
the Pi/PPi balance in the matrix vesicles is critical to the initiation of HA formation.
the balance between Pi and PPi, as well as the relative abundance of the two nucleotides, is a key determinant of mineralisation.
